questions.prompt: Click the Cerebellum on the 3D brain.
Which structure is primarily responsible for forming new long-term memories?
questions.explanation: The hippocampus, deep in the temporal lobe, is essential for converting short-term experiences into long-term memories.

questions.prompt: Click the Left Hippocampus on the 3D brain.
Which lobe contains the primary visual cortex?
questions.explanation: The occipital lobe, at the very back of the brain, is the brain's primary visual processing center.

questions.prompt: Damage to which structure is classically linked to major personality and impulse-control changes (as in the historical case of Phineas Gage)?
questions.explanation: The frontal lobe governs planning, impulse control, and personality — damage there can dramatically change behavior.

questions.prompt: Click the Brainstem on the 3D brain.
Which structure acts as the brain's main sensory relay station, passing nearly all sensory input to the cortex?
questions.explanation: Nearly all sensory information (except smell) is relayed through the thalamus before reaching the cortex.

questions.prompt: Which structure connects the left and right cerebral hemispheres, letting them share information?
questions.explanation: The corpus callosum is the brain's largest white matter structure, bridging the two hemispheres.
